sender.en: “FIA”, “Cyber Crime Wing” or “NCCIA”, with a case number, stamp and signature

name.en: Fake FIA notice: “a cybercrime case is registered against you, pay to avoid arrest”

how.en: A notice arrives on WhatsApp, by email or on social media in the name of the FIA. It looks official, with a case number, signature and stamp, and accuses you of a criminal or cyber law violation. It threatens arrest unless you pay a fine or “compensation” at once, or asks for personal and bank details for “verification”. The FIA says it never asks for bank details through calls or notices, and that a notice without a QR code should be treated as suspicious.

text.en: A notice arrives on WhatsApp or email in the FIA’s name.
It accuses you of a cybercrime and threatens arrest.
You are told to pay now to close the case.
You are told not to discuss it, and asked for personal and bank details.

FEDERAL INVESTIGATION AGENCY – CYBER CRIME. Notice: Case No. [number] has been registered against you under cyber crime law. You will be arrested within 24 hours unless the fine is deposited. Reply to this message to settle the case.
Official notice from FIA: your CNIC is involved in a money laundering inquiry. Share your bank account details for verification or legal action will be taken today.
